thread:
Maria Chen: heads up — opened a small PR to update the metering dashboard panel and add an SDK snippet for tiered pricing. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1428 :eyes:
Jamal Ortiz: thanks — can you paste the Python snippet here? want to validate the header examples for v2 SDK usage
Maria Chen: sure, here's the snippet I added to the PR:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=REDWOOD_KEY)
resp = client.usage.get_billing_breakdown(
    start="2026-02-01",
    end="2026-02-28",
    granularity="daily",
    tiers=["hosted","dedicated"]
)
print(resp)
```
Ben Kline: quick nit — the new SDK method is `usage.get_billing_breakdown`? I thought we settled on `billing.list_breakdown` in the SDK sync last month. Which version of the SDK docs are we targeting?
Maria Chen: good catch. PR currently targets docs v2 (the migration guide). I can switch to the `billing.list_breakdown` name to match the published SDK v0.9.1 examples.
Samira Patel: also, the Grafana panel in the PR references metric `redwood.quota_consumed`. CI linkchecker failed because metric got renamed to `redwood.quota.consumed` in telemetry. docs-bot posted a failure, see below.
docs-bot: linkcheck: broken link or metric key mismatch detected in files:
- docs/metrics/panels/metering-weekly.yaml: metric "redwood.quota_consumed" not found
- docs/sdks/python/usage-snippets.md: reference to /sdk/v2/usage -> 404
Jamal Ortiz: ok we need 3 small changes: 1) update SDK example to `billing.list_breakdown`, 2) change metric key in the Grafana YAML, 3) add a redirect from /sdk/v2/usage -> /sdk/python/usage (or update links). I can take the redirect if Maria updates snippets.
Maria Chen: assigning myself the snippet rename and link update. Will push a patch in ~30m. For the Grafana metric, Ben — can you confirm the correct metric name from telemetry?
Ben Kline: confirmed: `redwood.quota.consumed` is the canonical series. Also we now include a `tier` label, so the panel query should be `sum by(tier)(rate(redwood.quota.consumed[5m]))`. I'll paste a suggested YAML patch below.
Ben Kline: ```yaml
panels:
  - title: "Quota consumed by tier"
    query: "sum by(tier)(rate(redwood.quota.consumed[5m]))"
    legend: "{{tier}}"
    thresholds:
      - color: "#E24D42"
        value: 0.9
```
Samira Patel: that looks good. For the redirect, Jamal — do we want a short-lived redirect or update all internal references? We should avoid churn in the published guides.
Jamal Ortiz: prefer adding a redirect in the site config with a note in the PR. We'll keep the canonical page at /sdk/python/usage and mark /sdk/v2/usage as deprecated. Docs search will surface the new page.
Maria Chen: patch pushed: updated snippet to `billing.list_breakdown`, fixed the Python code, swapped metric name in the YAML, and added redirect entry in config/_redirects.yml. Ran local linkcheck and all good.
docs-bot: ci/linkcheck: passed for changed files (docs/sdks/python/usage-snippets.md, docs/metrics/panels/metering-weekly.yaml, config/_redirects.yml).
Samira Patel: awesome — can you add a tiny note in the metering guide about the `tier` label (how to interpret hosted vs dedicated) so product reads it? users keep asking how we partition costs.
Maria Chen: yep adding a 2-sentence explanatory note now. Also will add a short example Grafana query using `sum by(tier)` and example legend.
Jamal Ortiz: once CI is green, I'll merge and backport the redirect to the v1 branch. Thanks everyone. :tada:
Ben Kline: FYI I'm going to open a follow-up PR to add a short eval snippet showing how to compute effective unit price per-tier using the billing breakdown — low effort and helpful for customers.
Maria Chen: perfect — let's keep followups separate. merging now after final CI check.
